stories.headline: NASA ponders a Hubble servicing mission or a controlled deorbit
stories.claim: NASA has issued a request for information on servicing or deorbiting Hubble, as its orbit decays and reentry risk rises.
stories.summary: NASA has posted a request for information asking commercial space companies how they could service the Hubble Space Telescope. The agency estimates a 10 per cent chance Hubble re-enters the atmosphere by September 2032, rising to 50 per cent by December 2033. Options include a controlled deorbit, boosting the telescope to a higher orbit of at least 600 km, or enhancing its performance and lifetime. NASA requires any mission by 2032 and says it must not harm the telescope. No budget has been stated, and this is an information-gathering step rather than a request for proposals.

stories.headline: AI projects not paying off? Keep at it, says Uni Productivity Institute
stories.claim: A Productivity Institute report says AI's productivity gains are lagging because firms' up-front costs and task-level gains take time to translate into business results.
stories.summary: The Register reports on 'The AI Ambition Gap', a report from the University of Manchester's Productivity Institute, commissioned by IT services firm Bytes Technology Group. The report examines why widespread AI adoption has not yet produced the productivity gains forecast. It argues that up-front investment in retraining and reorganisation pays back only later, and that task-level gains do not automatically become gains for whole roles or firms. It cites examples such as software developers completing about 26 percent more tasks with GitHub Copilot, and a finding that AI dev tools raised coding activity far more than actual software releases. The UK is said to have the highest share of workers in high-exposure, high-complementarity occupations among six countries compared. The report recommends management focus, skills and workflow redesign, and it notes that other reports this week were more pessimistic.
key_points: The Productivity Institute at the University of Manchester published 'The AI Ambition Gap', commissioned by Bytes Technology Group.
Up-front investment in staff retraining and reorganisation shows costs immediately, while benefits arrive later.
Task-level efficiency gains do not automatically raise productivity across whole roles or organisations.
Coding activity rose sharply with AI dev tools, but software releases grew far less because human checking remains necessary.
The UK has the highest share of workers in AI-exposed, complementary occupations among the countries compared, per the report.
Other reports this week, including one from Gartner, were more sceptical about AI productivity payoffs.
stories.market_take: Limited direct market impact; mainly a research report on AI adoption, with Bytes Technology Group as the commissioning firm.

stories.summary: India's space agency ISRO launched the NVS-03 navigation satellite on its GSLV-F18 rocket from Sriharikota on Friday, 30 October 2026. The rocket placed the 2,250 kg satellite into its intended geosynchronous transfer orbit about 18 minutes after liftoff. ISRO chairman V. Narayanan confirmed the success. Following NVS-03, ISRO would need at least two more NVS-series satellites to restore minimum operational capacity. The NVS-02 satellite, launched in January 2025, failed to raise its orbit after engine problems.

stories.headline: A new vulnerability can brick your Android phone when receiving the SMS of Death
stories.claim: Researcher reports an Android flaw where a specially crafted WAP Push SMS can disrupt or brick phones running Android 12 or later.
stories.summary: Security researcher Mark Blaszczyk has disclosed a vulnerability affecting Android 12 and later, in which a specially crafted WAP Push SMS is processed in the background rather than shown to the user. The flaw can drop calls, cut cellular service temporarily and, with repeated messages, render a device unusable, with recovery often needing technical support. No user action is required. Google initially denied the issue when it was reported in May, but a fix is included in the October 2026 security patch for Android 14 and later, while older devices remain exposed. Users on Android 13 or older have few options.
key_points: The flaw affects all devices running Android 12 or later, and has been seen on Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones so far.
A malicious WAP Push SMS is processed in the background, so no user interaction is needed.
Effects include dropped calls, temporary loss of cellular service and, with multiple messages, a potentially unusable device.
Google denied the issue when reported in May, but its engineers added a fix in the October 2026 security patch for Android 14 and later.
Android 13 and older devices remain vulnerable, and users should install the October patch if they can.
stories.market_take: Limited direct market effect; a reputational issue for Google and Samsung.

Both probes are nearing their 50th anniversary in 2027 and are running on very limited power.

stories.headline: HTTP/3 is faster with some work and help from Cloudflare
stories.claim: Delivery Hero cut app latency by moving most users to HTTP/3 with Cloudflare, sharing engineering results from a conference talk.
stories.summary: At the P99 2026 virtual conference, a Delivery Hero engineer described how the Germany-based delivery company moved most of its users to HTTP/3. The change cut total end-to-end response time on the home screen by 17%, and P95 read latency fell from 1.2 seconds to 120 milliseconds. Setup on the Cloudflare CDN was simple, but Android needed custom work, including a forked Cronet bridge, to cut initialisation delays. Around 95% of users were moved to HTTP/3, with the rest falling back to HTTP/2. A remaining issue with packet loss in markets such as Pakistan is being worked on with Cloudflare. Separately, Uber is acquiring Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion.
key_points: Delivery Hero moved about 95% of its users to HTTP/3, falling back to HTTP/2 where UDP is blocked.

stories.headline: Smoke from wildfires killed 3,500 people in Indonesia in September: Report
stories.claim: A CREA report says toxic smoke from wildfires killed about 3,560 people in Indonesia in September 2026.
stories.summary: A report from the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), released on Thursday, estimates that air pollution deaths in Indonesia rose 42 percent in September, to 5,310 from 3,740 in August. Of the September total, about 3,560 deaths were attributed to toxic smoke from forest and land fires, and about 1,750 to urban and industrial pollution. Fire smoke accounted for 94 to 99 percent of deaths in Kalimantan and over 80 percent on Sumatra. The number of people exposed to unhealthy or hazardous air reached a record 58 million in September. The fires, worsened by El Nino drought, have also affected Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor, and the Jakarta government is facing criticism over its response.
key_points: CREA estimates 3,560 deaths in September from wildfire smoke in Indonesia, out of 5,310 air pollution deaths that month.
Air pollution deaths rose 42 percent from an estimated 3,740 in August.
Fire smoke caused 94 to 99 percent of deaths in Kalimantan and over 80 percent on Sumatra.
Exposure to unhealthy-to-hazardous air hit a record 58 million people in September.
An El Nino drought fuelled the fires, which also affected Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor.
The Indonesian government says it deployed over 72,000 personnel, activated 2,100 health workers and distributed 5.3 million masks.
stories.market_take: Prolonged haze could weigh modestly on Indonesian plantation and mining operations, but no clear listed-stock impact is reported.

stories.headline: The proof that Putin exploited Ukraine’s Starlink blackout
stories.claim: Telegraph analysis links a pause in US intelligence and Starlink access to a surge in Russian strikes on Ukraine.
stories.summary: A Telegraph analysis, using CSIS data, finds Russia launched about 4,003 strikes between 12 and 24 October, up 58 percent from 2,527 in the preceding 12 days. This followed a pause in US intelligence sharing reported by Zelensky on 13 October, and restrictions on Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield, which Elon Musk said was imposed over terms-of-service violations. Ukraine's interception rate fell from 87 percent to 84.9 percent, and to 77.8 percent on one day. Russia also increased its use of faster jet-powered Geran drones. The restrictions reportedly lasted until 24 October, and the Kremlin is said to have tried to portray Ukraine's negotiating position as weak.

stories.headline: Indians turn to start-ups to care for ageing parents as young become more mobile
stories.claim: Indian start-ups are growing to meet rising demand for elderly care as young adults move away from family homes.
stories.summary: A BBC feature looks at how Indian families are turning to start-ups for elder care as younger people move away and joint families shrink. NITI Aayog values India's senior care industry at about $7bn (around £5.56bn), and Colliers estimates senior living demand at 2 to 2.2 million units against roughly 25,000 available. Firms such as Manasum Senior Living, Goodfellows, NoBlink.ai and Emoha are offering senior housing, home care, companionship and AI monitoring. Key challenges include affordability, a shortage of trained caregivers and fraud risks. NITI Aayog has called for a national caregiving policy.

stories.claim: UK defence secretary announces offset rules requiring foreign firms winning £50m+ contracts to invest equal value in Britain.
stories.summary: The UK government has announced new 'offset' rules requiring foreign defence contractors awarded UK contracts worth more than £50m to spend an equivalent amount on British factories, jobs and training. The Ministry of Defence will apply the rules case by case from April 2027, and the government says similar schemes exist in Poland, Norway and the Netherlands. The announcement comes amid political pressure over how the UK will reach its target of 3% of GDP on defence by 2030, with key spending decisions deferred to next year's spending review. Critics including Labour's Tan Dhesi and Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch say the government is delaying necessary decisions.

stories.headline: Oil flows are up as Iran war turmoil eases. Why do prices keep rising?
stories.claim: Oil flows from the Gulf have recovered, yet Brent prices near $117 remain elevated due to supply risks and depleted stocks.
stories.summary: Oil exports from the Gulf rose to an average of 24.6 million barrels per day in the week to 18 October, above the pre-war average, according to Kpler. Brent crude front-month futures rose more than 2% on Friday to briefly top $117 a barrel, their highest since April and more than 60% above pre-war levels. Analysts say prices reflect fears of renewed hostilities, shrinking stockpiles and high freight costs, which reached as much as $40 a barrel, about ten times the usual rate. Shipping has shifted to ship-to-ship transfers and bypass pipelines, but the IEA says OPEC Gulf output in September was only 75% of its pre-war level and global stocks are 509 million barrels below pre-war levels. Brent for October 2027 delivery traded above $90, suggesting markets expect a prolonged squeeze.

By comparison, incomes grew about 12% in the 2010s. Energy costs are expected to rise by around £400 per household between October 2026 and July 2027 because of the energy shock linked to the Iran war, while Budget measures are expected to save a typical family about £140 over the same period. The report comes after John Healey's first Budget, which the opposition criticised for weak growth, higher taxes and unclear defence funding. Political tension is also rising over speculation about an early election.
key_points: The IFS expects UK household disposable income to grow only about 2% over the 2020s.
This is the weakest income growth in the period the IFS analysed, covering each decade since the 1950s.
Energy costs are estimated to rise about £400 per household from October 2026 to July 2027.
Budget measures are expected to save a typical family around £140 over the same period.
The shadow chancellor called the Budget a missed opportunity, and the defence funding plan was delayed until next year's Spending Review.
Ministers deny plans for an early election, but speculation persists.
stories.market_take: Weak household income growth could weigh on consumer spending and UK domestic-facing shares.

stories.headline: The U.S. expected 17,000 disputes a year when it passed this medical bills law. It gets over 2 million instead
stories.claim: A health policy expert says the No Surprises Act's arbitration process is driving up insurance costs, with providers winning most disputes.
stories.summary: A US health policy researcher and former federal official argues that the No Surprises Act, in force since 2022, has protected patients from most surprise out-of-network bills, with about 50 million such bills prevented by September 2026. However, the arbitration process for out-of-network payment disputes is pushing up premiums for employers and individuals. Providers win roughly 85 per cent of disputes, and arbitrators often choose offers well above in-network rates and Medicare. The federal government had expected around 17,000 disputes a year, but the figure is over 2 million. Rules to strengthen the arbitration benchmark were blocked by provider lawsuits. The author calls for action to address the problem.

stories.headline: Experts adopt AI agent's random opinions and think they're their own, Anthropic study finds
stories.claim: Anthropic study finds experts adopted an AI agent's randomly assigned preferences and mostly believed the conclusions were their own.
stories.summary: An Anthropic experiment with 50 causal-inference experts found that participants adopted the AI agent's assigned preference in 86 percent of four analytical decisions, far above chance. The agent had been given a coin-toss preference and only made honest arguments for its side. Most participants still felt the final recommendation was their own, and 77 percent used the agent's arguments in their explanations. The researchers warn that shared default AI preferences could create false consensus in science and weaken human checks on AI safety research. AI-assisted analyses also had far fewer serious flaws, 6 percent against 55 percent without AI.
key_points: Experts adopted the agent's randomly assigned preference in 86 percent of four analytical decisions.
Most participants believed the final recommendation was mostly or entirely their own.
77 percent used at least one of the agent's arguments in their explanations, often in nearly the same words.
AI-assisted analyses had serious flaws in 6 percent of cases, compared with 55 percent without AI.

stories.summary: Adidas reported record third-quarter sales of €7.3 billion, up 7% on a constant currency basis, with operating profit up 37% to €1 billion. Direct-to-consumer sales rose 17% while wholesale grew only 2% as the company limited distribution and cut discounting. Apparel grew 19%, footwear was flat and Europe fell 4%. Adidas now expects 9-10% revenue growth in 2026 and operating profit of €2.5 billion, including a €200 million tariff refund. Outgoing CFO Harm Ohlmeyer will be succeeded by Birgit Kretschmer.
key_points: Q3 sales reached a record €7.3bn, up 7% at constant currency.
Operating profit rose 37% to €1bn, beating the prior quarter.
Direct-to-consumer sales grew 17%, while wholesale rose only 2%.
Apparel grew 19% while footwear stayed flat at €3.8bn.
Full-year 2026 operating profit guidance rises to €2.5bn from €2.3bn, including a €200m tariff refund.
CFO Harm Ohlmeyer will be succeeded by Birgit Kretschmer.
stories.market_take: Raised guidance and a strong profit beat are positive for Adidas shares, though Europe weakness and footwear stagnation are concerns.

stories.headline: Molecular chirality wins this year’s Nobel Prize in Chemistry - The Johns Hopkins News-Letter
stories.claim: Kagan and Soai awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on non-linear effects and autocatalysis in chirality.
stories.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry on 7 October to Henri Kagan of Université Paris-Saclay and Kenso Soai of Tokyo University of Science. The prize recognises their discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric synthesis, which allow chemists to amplify one 'handed' form of a molecule. The article explains why this matters for pharmaceuticals, citing the thalidomide tragedy, and for origin-of-life research. The prize is 12 million Swedish kronor, about $1.21 million, shared equally between the two laureates.
key_points: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was announced on 7 October for work on asymmetric synthesis.
Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai share the prize equally.
Kagan's work shows how slightly uneven catalyst mixtures can produce very different product ratios.
Soai showed a reaction whose product acts as its own catalyst, known as asymmetric autocatalysis.
The discoveries matter for drug design, since mirror-image forms of a molecule can behave very differently.
The prize is worth 12 million Swedish kronor, around $1.21 million.

stories.headline: Battle lines redrawn in Spain’s snap election after latest train disaster
stories.claim: Spain's snap election campaign is reshaped after a deadly high-speed rail crash that killed at least 69 people near Urda.
stories.summary: A deadly high-speed rail collision on Wednesday near Urda, which killed at least 69 people, has reshaped Spain's snap general election due next month. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who called the poll after the housing reforms were voted down, now has to defend the government's rail safety record. The crash follows another on the same line in January that killed 46 people. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo of the PP and the far-right Vox are both attacking the government, with Vox urging the supreme court to investigate transport minister Óscar Puente. Analysts say the national mood of mourning could make it harder for Sánchez to mobilise left-leaning voters.

Vox has urged the supreme court to investigate transport minister Óscar Puente; Puente denies mismanagement.
Political scientist Pablo Simón says the mood of mourning may make it hard to mobilise around 1.2 million politically dormant PSOE-leaning voters.

stories.headline: Intel shares sink as memory shortage drags its PC chip outlook
stories.claim: Intel shares fell over 20% after forecasting weak fourth-quarter revenue, hit by a PC memory shortage and data centre supply problems.
stories.summary: Intel shares fell more than 20% in late trading on Thursday after the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15bn to $16bn, below the $17bn analysts expected. It also guided to adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share against estimates of 43 cents. Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blamed a shortage of memory chips that has pushed up prices and cut PC demand, plus supply problems in the data centre unit, including raw material shortages and a factory shutdown in Israel. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year and 10% in 2027. Third-quarter revenue rose 21% to $16.5bn, with data centre and AI sales up 78% to $7.3bn. The stock had more than doubled this year.

stories.headline: Traders' tools stolen every 20 minutes in UK
stories.claim: Tool thefts in the UK were recorded roughly every 20 minutes in 2025, with at least 26,164 reported across 30 forces.

Tradespeople describe heavy costs, with replacing a van's tools up to £7,000 and repairs of £4,000-£5,000, and insurance claims often falling short of replacement costs.

The central bank kept its key interest rate unchanged at 1.25%, with an eight-to-one vote, after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank held rates earlier in the week. The BoJ warned that core CPI excluding fresh food is likely to accelerate to clearly above 2%, citing energy and goods prices, chip prices linked to AI demand and yen weakness. Core inflation in September was 2.1%. Analysts expect further tightening, with Capital Economics forecasting a 2% policy rate by mid-next-year, while Japanese officials are expected to hike in December.

stories.headline: Topcoat enables Rust to render server-side web apps
stories.claim: Carl Lerche of AWS presented Topcoat, a Rust framework that renders server-side web apps, at ScyllaDB's P99 conference.
stories.summary: Carl Lerche, an Amazon Web Services principal engineer and creator of the Tokio runtime, presented Topcoat at ScyllaDB's 2026 P99 virtual conference. Topcoat is a framework for building web applications in Rust. It compiles Rust into JavaScript rather than WebAssembly, and most logic runs on the server, with only results sent to the browser. Lerche said it suits typical database-driven web apps rather than very complex applications. It draws on server-side rendering approaches such as HTMX, Datastar and Phoenix LiveView, and connects components directly to the database through his Toasty project. Ken Kohlman, a frontend developer, praised its simplicity while noting it only supports a subset of Rust syntax.

stories.headline: Someone ran Rivian’s pedal-by-wire e-bike out of battery and things got weird
stories.claim: A owner's test of the ALSO TM-B pedal-by-wire e-bike found it keeps limited assistance on low battery but had odd behaviour and heavy overnight drain.
stories.summary: An early Launch Edition owner, Aaron Draczynski, ran the ALSO TM-B e-bike down to empty to test its pedal-by-wire system and shared the results on YouTube. As the battery fell, the bike progressively cut its maximum assist, down to Level 1, before electric assistance stopped at 4% charge. The bike then entered what the owner called Infinite Turtle Mode, where pedalling energy is passed through the electronic drivetrain. He said it was workable on flat ground but very hard on hills, with manual shifting disabled. Separately, the bike drained from 70% to 18% over about two days while parked, and then showed a battery error that a physical reset button fixed. The owner suspects the lack of a cell signal may be the cause.

The AGs said more than 370,000 drivers were wrongly told they were not enrolled, and their data was still sold. Under the settlement, GM must limit the driving data it collects and protect personal information, and it faces mandated privacy assessments and staff training. The settlement follows a Federal Trade Commission ban earlier this year on sharing certain consumer data for five years, and a $12.75 million settlement with California in May.

stories.headline: What is it like to work when your co-workers are AI agents?

AI startup Anything has around 15 human staff and roughly 150 agents, and its founder expects AI co-workers to outnumber humans at most companies within a year. stories.headline: How the UK’s 2026 Budget Will Impact Fashion
stories.claim: The UK Budget has been delivered with modest measures for fashion retail and mixed reactions from the industry.
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey delivered the UK Budget on Wednesday, and fashion industry responses have been lukewarm, describing it as a 'first, do no harm' budget. The small business rates relief threshold rises from £12,000 to £18,000 for retail, hospitality and leisure, which Treasury says will take around 70,000 businesses off business rates. An entrepreneurs' capital gains tax relief gives a 10% rate on up to £10 million of lifetime gains. However, the national living wage and national minimum wage both rise 3.9%, above inflation of 3.5%. Luxury retailers such as Harvey Nichols, Selfridges and Harrods are seen as disadvantaged, according to PwC's retail head.
key_points: The Budget raises the small business rates relief threshold from £12,000 to £18,000 for retail, hospitality and leisure.
About 70,000 businesses will stop paying business rates, according to the Budget presentation.
Entrepreneurs' capital gains tax relief offers 10% on up to £10 million of lifetime gains.
Living wage and national minimum wage both rise 3.9%, above 3.5% inflation.
Industry bodies welcomed the measures but said they largely help independent shops, while luxury department stores are seen as disadvantaged.
stories.market_take: Limited direct effect on listed fashion groups; the wage rise adds cost pressure for UK retailers.

stories.headline: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: to nail this year’s British heritage look, just study Rivals
stories.claim: Guardian feature says British heritage style, inspired by the TV drama Rivals, is in vogue this autumn.
stories.summary: A Guardian fashion column argues that British heritage dressing, including waxed jackets, tweed, tartan and wellies, is having a moment this autumn. The writer credits the new Rivals adaptation, based on Jilly Cooper's novel, with reviving the Sloane Ranger look, citing costume designer Ray Holman's use of 1980s Dunhill and Mulberry pieces. The piece suggests mixing practical outerwear with glamour and gives styling tips and high-street prices from Marks & Spencer, Aligne, Me + Em, Dune and Pilgrim.
key_points: Tartan, tweed, waxed jackets and wellies are described as a current style trend.
The Rivals TV series has revived interest in old-school British dressing.
Costume designer Ray Holman drew on original 1980s pieces from Dunhill and Mulberry.
The column recommends pairing utilitarian items with glamour, such as a waxed jacket over a party dress.
Styling credits list high-street and mid-market brands including Marks & Spencer and Dune.

stories.headline: Firefox Reunites Iconic Early Internet Memes to Push Back Against Modern AI
stories.claim: Firefox has launched an advert reuniting early internet personalities to criticise intrusive tracking and built-in AI.
stories.summary: Mozilla's Firefox browser has released a nostalgic commercial featuring ten viral figures from the early internet. The creators question intrusive data tracking and the spread of built-in artificial intelligence in software. The campaign promotes Firefox's privacy features, including an integrated VPN and a setting that minimises AI tools.
key_points: The advert features ten early internet personalities.
It criticises intrusive data tracking and the growing presence of AI features.
Firefox highlights an integrated VPN and a toggle to reduce AI tools.
The campaign is a marketing effort by the browser maker.
